_note: v2 hook overrides for le port, used only where the source hook breaks the content rules or differs from the painting. Source data is untouched.

fr_capitaine_noun.hook: The white-bearded ship's CAPTAIN tips his CAP to the row of seagulls on the blue rail: "We sail at TEN!" CAP-IT-TEN = CAPITAINE.
fr_capitaine_noun.why: The source respelling trips the content scan (\bpee\b); the cue is now CAP-IT-TEN. Matches the captain saluting the gulls.

fr_voile_noun_f.hook: A gust fills the big orange-striped SAIL and the bearded sailor in his yellow life jacket grins from the tiller: "VOILÀ!" (VWAHL) as the dinghy leaps forward.
fr_voile_noun_f.why: In the painting the sailor sits at the tiller grinning; he does not throw up an arm.

fr_barque_noun.hook: A brown dog sits in the SMALL rowing BOAT next to a boy at the oars and BARKS (BAHRK) at a white duck paddling alongside.
fr_barque_noun.why: The dog sits beside the boy rowing; the duck is in the water next to the boat.

fr_port_noun.hook: The walrus harbor master carries a basket of silver sardines from his little blue kiosk, ready to POUR (POR) them out for the gulls: welcome to the PORT.
fr_port_noun.why: The walrus is holding the full basket, about to pour, not pouring.

fr_navire_noun.hook: Out at sea a great steamSHIP has to VEER (nah-VEER) sharply round a little seagull bobbing in its path.
fr_navire_noun.why: The painting shows a seagull on the water in front of the steamship, not a duck.

fr_filet_noun.hook: A young fisherman hauls up the green NET, and a fat gray seal lies asleep inside it as if he had paid a FEE (fee-LEH) for the hammock.
fr_filet_noun.why: The net is hauled by a boy; grammar fixed (lies, not lays).

fr_equipage_noun.hook: The fishing boat's CREW lines up on deck in sailor caps, and the cabin boy at the end holds up A golden KEY (ay-kee-PAHZH).
fr_equipage_noun.why: Matches the four crew in caps and the cabin boy raising the key.

fr_bac_noun.hook: A student with a big BACKpack (BAHK) rides on the deck of the little FERRY chugging past the breakwater.
fr_bac_noun.why: The student stands with his backpack; he is not reading.

fr_flotte_noun.hook: A FLEET of little toy-colored rowing boats FLOATS (FLOT) together in a cluster by the shore.
fr_flotte_noun.why: The boats are a cluster, not a six-boat parade line.

fr_rame_noun.hook: A woolly horned RAM (RAHM) sits in the toy blue rowing boat on the rack, pulling one big wooden OAR.
fr_rame_noun.why: The ram is a toy on the rack; two real oars lean beside him.

fr_exploration_noun.hook: A red crab in a pith helmet sets off with his lantern and his rolled-out map on an EXPLORATION of the rack (ehk-sploh-rah-SYOHN).
fr_exploration_noun.why: The crab is on the bottom shelf next to a lantern and a map.

fr_mousse_noun_m.hook: A MOOSE (MOOS) dressed as the SHIP'S BOY, in a striped sailor shirt and little cap, mops the top shelf of the rack.
fr_mousse_noun_m.why: The moose mops the shelf, not the pontoon.

fr_porteur_noun.hook: The PORTER in red carries a tower of suitcases high above his head, a green parrot on top and an umbrella under his arm (por-TUHR).
fr_porteur_noun.why: The porter holds the stacked cases up overhead with an umbrella.

fr_paquebot_noun.hook: The model white LINER on the bottom shelf is a PACKED BOAT (pah-kuh-BOH): every deck is crammed with waving tourists.
fr_paquebot_noun.why: The liner is a model on the luggage rack.

fr_ancre_noun.hook: A black iron ANCHOR drops on its chain from the little blue boat, and a crab rides it down (AHNKR) while another crab waves from the boat.
fr_ancre_noun.why: Two crabs are painted: one on the anchor, one in the boat.

fr_navigation_noun.hook: NAVIGATION by seagull: from its rock a gull shows the way, and a line of five ducklings swims after it (nah-vee-gah-SYOHN).
fr_navigation_noun.why: Matches the gull on its rock and the five ducklings.

fr_navigateur_noun.hook: A penguin NAVIGATOR in a captain's cap stands at a ship's wheel on the jetty, holding up his map (nah-vee-gah-TUHR).
fr_navigateur_noun.why: The penguin holds the map up beside the wheel.

fr_arrivant_noun.hook: A boy ARRIVING (ah-ree-VAHN) on the jetty, his old suitcase in one hand and a big bunch of welcome flowers in the other: a NEWCOMER!
fr_arrivant_noun.why: Masculine noun: the painted arrivant is a smiling boy, not a woman.

fr_pirogue_noun.hook: A ROGUE green pea in a pirate hat and eyepatch paddles a little wooden dugout CANOE across the cove (PEA-ROGUE).
fr_pirogue_noun.why: Content scan flags the standalone respelling; the memory cue is now written as PEA-ROGUE.

fr_detroit_noun.hook: A red car from DETROIT (day-TRWAH) rides a little ferry through the narrow STRAIT between the island cliffs and the harbor wall.
fr_detroit_noun.why: The ferry passes between the palm-island cliffs and the stone harbor wall.

fr_naufrage_noun.hook: A ragged CASTAWAY sits under the palm tree on his tiny island with a pile of coconuts and sighs: "NO FRIDGE (noh-frah-ZHAY), just coconuts."
fr_naufrage_noun.why: He sits under the palm with the coconuts; no mention of a shipwreck, which is not painted.

fr_explorateur_noun.hook: A young EXPLORER in a pith helmet stands in his little sailboat, scanning the cove through a long brass telescope (ehk-sploh-rah-TUHR).
fr_explorateur_noun.why: The explorer painted is a young one in a sailboat.

fr_nautique_adj.hook: A parrot in a NAUTICAL sailor cap ties a big rope knot on the old boat on the sand: NO TICK (noh-TEEK) of the clock wasted.
fr_nautique_adj.why: The boat is upright on the sand, not upturned.

fr_container_noun.hook: Behind the otters' sailboat a little CONTAINER ship chugs past, stacked with colorful boxes like giant building blocks (kohn-teh-NEHR).
fr_container_noun.why: Le container is masculine (vocab.jsonl has it feminine), so the ship was moved from the left half of the jetée painting to the right half; the hook now says where it is.

fr_petrolier_adj.hook: Sounds like 'PETROLeum, YAY!' (pay-troh-LYAY): on the shed shelf sits a toy oil TANKER ship (un navire pétrolier) with a black oil-drop on its red hull, the ship that carries PETROLEUM.
fr_petrolier_adj.why: Paint-back (sparse rule): plan-only since p12 (from route/parking), was planned port/jetee (full at 14); re-planned to the port shed zoom (R_harbour_01 / R_harbour_01_z1), and the rolled map on the middle shelf was repainted as a toy oil tanker (center band, since it is an adjective). bagages goes from 5 to 6.

fr_bateau_noun.hook: BAT + TOE: a BAT in a sailor hat steers the red BOAT by the tiller with its TOE (bah-TOH).
fr_bateau_noun.why: Pack C v2 (approved, 2b039891): the bat steers the red boat by its tiller at the stern with its foot.

fr_vigie_noun.hook: "vee-ZHEE": the lookout up in the crow's nest is a giant VEGGIE, a carrot: vee-ZHEE = VEGGIE
fr_vigie_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a person in a giant carrot costume up in the crow's nest, hands cupped round the eyes, on the lookout. Gate 29 second sense.
fr_vigie_noun.note: A lookout (the person or the post); also a watchdog group.

fr_boussole_noun.hook: "boo-SOL": a pirate shows the compass stuck to his BOOT SOLE: boo-SOL = BOOT-SOLE
fr_boussole_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a laughing pirate holding up his boot with a brass compass stuck to the sole.

fr_cargaison_noun.hook: "kar-geh-ZOHN": in the cargo crates sits a toy CAR the children GAZE ON: kar-geh-ZOHN = CAR-GAZE-ON
fr_cargaison_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): two dress-up children gazing at a shiny red toy car on top of a stack of cargo crates and sacks.

fr_cale_noun.hook: "KAHL": a sailor CALLS down through the hatch into the dark hold: KAHL = CALL
fr_cale_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a sailor kneeling at an open deck hatch, hands cupped, calling down into the dark hold. Gate 29 second sense.
fr_cale_noun.note: The hold of a ship; also a wedge put under a wobbly table leg.

fr_gouvernail_noun.hook: "goo-vehr-NIGH": the helmsman GOVERNs the ship from the big wheel, the harbor drawing NIGH: goo-vehr-NIGH = GOVERN-NIGH
fr_gouvernail_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a determined helmsman in a tricorn hat gripping two spokes of the big wooden ship's wheel and steering.

fr_mat_noun.hook: "MAH": a pirate's MA lovingly hugs the tall mast: MAH = MA
fr_mat_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a smiling mother in a headscarf hugging the base of the tall wooden mast.

fr_corsaire_noun.hook: "kor-SEHR": like English CORSAIR: the dashing privateer in a plumed hat points out to sea: kor-SEHR = CORSAIR
fr_corsaire_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a dashing privateer captain in a plumed tricorn hat and long blue coat pointing ahead from the bow.

fr_brigand_noun.hook: "bree-GAHN": a mischievous bandit grins from the ship's BRIG: bree-GAHN = BRIG-GONE
fr_brigand_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a mischievous grinning bandit in a red bandana waving from behind the bars of the ship's little brig. Moved from the wall-text room R_text_crime_03 (where it was only a blank plaque) into this painted room.

fr_hublot_noun.hook: "ew-BLOH": a girl at the porthole goes 'OO' and BLOWS soap bubbles: ew-BLOH = OO-BLOW
fr_hublot_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a girl looking out of a round brass porthole blowing soap bubbles.

fr_pirate_noun.hook: "pea-RAHT": a tiny pirate RAT nibbles a PEA on a barrel: pea-RAHT = PEA-RAT
fr_pirate_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a little gray rat in a red pirate bandana sitting on a barrel holding one big green pea.

fr_butin_noun.hook: "bew-TAN": the pirates' loot sack is full of giant BUTTONS: bew-TAN = BUTTON
fr_butin_noun.why: English sound-alike painted in musee/bateau_pirate (Oct 31 2026 Musée fix pack; room moved to port/bateau_pirate in batch 7, painting kept): a pirate kid in a red bandana opening a loot sack overflowing with giant colorful buttons. Gate 29 second sense.
fr_butin_noun.note: Loot, booty; also any haul you collect, like a child's Halloween candy haul.
